name: Revenge of Gann
summary: At Bael Modan, Gann Stonespire turns the dwarves’ own plans against their flying machine. The Horde agent seeks revenge for the fallen Stonespire tribe.

sections.title: A Symbol of Domination
sections.body: At Bael Modan, the dwarven excavation sits atop the ancestral grounds of the displaced Stonespire tauren. The Prospectors rely on a gyrocopter for their reach and military strength. It is stationed on a watchtower above the dig, where it surveys the surrounding Barrens and protects the dwarves’ supply lines. For Gann, the machine also marks the Alliance’s intrusion into kalimdorian soil.

sections.title: Turned Upon Its Makers
sections.body: After recovering Prospector Khazgorm’s plans, Gann Stonespire makes a specialized charge called the Explosive Stick of Gann. Planting it on the flying machine turns the dwarves’ own invention against them. The blast destroys a vital military asset, humiliates the Bael'dun contingent, and honors the spirits of Gann’s lost tribe.

faq.q: Why does Gann want to destroy the flying machine specifically?
faq.answer: The flying machine aids Bael Modan’s infrastructure and gives the dwarves aerial reconnaissance. To Gann, it also embodies dwarven power and looms over land his slaughtered tribe once called home.

faq.q: Where is the flying machine located at Bael Modan?
faq.answer: The flying machine sits on a wooden tower platform halfway down the ramp into the main excavation pit, apart from the primary dwarven fortress.

faq.q: How did Gann create the explosive device?
faq.answer: Gann made the Explosive Stick of Gann from technical schematics and engineering plans recovered from Prospector Khazgorm, using the dwarves’ own designs against them.

faq.q: What tribe does Gann belong to?
faq.answer: Gann belongs to the Stonespire tribe, a tauren clan that once lived in the southern Barrens. The Ironforge dwarven excavation drove them out by force and destroyed their settlement.

faq.q: Does destroying the machine stop the excavation permanently?
faq.answer: Destroying the machine cripples Bael Modan’s air strength and infrastructure and gives Gann personal revenge. The heavily entrenched dwarven diggers and fortress remain an active Alliance stronghold in the region.

faq.q: What recognition does Gann offer upon finishing this mission?
faq.answer: Gann says the hero who destroyed the machine will be revered in Thunder Bluff as a defender of sacred tauren lands and a lasting champion of his lost tribe.

angles.text: Destroying dwarven war machines to avenge the Stonespire clan resonates with any tauren defending their ancestral homeland from desecration.
Crippling Bael Modan’s flying machine weakens an Alliance aerial weapon that can scout and strike deep into the southern Barrens.
The explosive turns Ironforge blueprints against a gyrocopter, making it a clever act of field sabotage.
